role: APPARENT compressive layer modulus of soft tissue under real load, in vivo -- the quantity a per-patch elastic foundation needs and the canonical skin layers do not carry (they declare E = 3000 Pa, a source_informed_prior over 0.5-30 kPa, identically for epidermis, dermis and hypodermis)
retrieved: 2026-09-10, from the publishers' abstracts and PMC full text

entries.citation: Teng Z-L, Yang X-G, Geng X, et al. Effect of loading history on material properties of human heel pad: an in-vivo pilot investigation during gait. BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2022;23:254.
entries.method: in vivo, during gait; Kelvin-Voigt fit of pressure against thickness strain
entries.also_cites: Gefen et al. 2001, in vivo heel pad elastic modulus as high as 175 kPa, viscosity 22 kPa s

entries.citation: Yang X-G, Teng Z-L, Zhang Z-M, et al. Comparison of material properties of heel pad between adults with and without type 2 diabetes history: an in-vivo investigation during gait. Front Endocrinol 2022;13:894383.
entries.method: in vivo, during gait; modified Kelvin-Voigt fit; NON-diabetic group, n = 10 (20 legs), aged 59-72
entries.apparent_modulus_check: 144.8 kPa / 0.523 = 277 kPa against the reported 265.5 kPa (4% apart): the modulus is pressure over THICKNESS strain, i.e. a layer (apparent) modulus, so k = E/h and the confined-layer factor (1-v)/((1+v)(1-2v)) must NOT be applied on top

entries.site: buttock subcutaneous fat, under the ischial tuberosity, sitting
entries.citation: Linder-Ganz E, Shabshin N, Itzchak Y, Gefen A. Assessment of mechanical conditions in sub-dermal tissues during sitting: a combined experimental-MRI and finite element approach. J Biomech 2007;40(7):1443-1454.
entries.method: in vivo MRI, weight-bearing vs non-weight-bearing, subject-specific FE; n = 6 healthy
entries.caveat: peak PRINCIPAL values from an FE model driven by MRI displacements, not a layer pressure over a thickness strain; the secant 18/0.46 = 39 kPa is therefore a transferred apparent modulus, weaker evidence than the heel values

not_found: no in vivo apparent compressive modulus retrieved for the forefoot/toes, knee, hand, forearm, elbow, shoulder or trunk soft tissue
